rationale_summary: Only 14.49% of assets have positive five-session returns, with 2.37 percentage points of active-return dispersion. The Fed hike, higher inflation projections and stronger dollar provide substantive reasons for weakness, not a blanket reversal signal. Nevertheless, resilient spending and capital investment argue against treating the largest industrial-demand-sensitive pullbacks as evidence of collapsing demand. Selective reversals have a modest edge, with substantial uncertainty and no assumption that pre-entry rebounds remain available after September 17.
portfolio_rationale: The leading candidates combine substantial relative pullbacks with independent evidence that economic demand remains resilient; Korea also has limited contemporaneous equity-market confirmation. Their reversal probabilities only narrowly clear the eligibility threshold. The ranking does not treat quality scores as business fundamentals or mechanically reward recent winners. Other pullbacks lack sufficient support to qualify, while municipal bonds offer defense rather than an overreaction trade.
key_risks: Further upward repricing of US rates and the dollar could overwhelm reversal demand across all three leading candidates.; Korea, copper and mining share global cyclical exposure, so their losses could be strongly correlated despite different instruments.; The September 17 entry close may already incorporate the Korean rebound and post-Fed stabilization, leaving less subsequent upside.; Industrial production on September 18 and new-home sales on September 24 could undermine the resilient-demand thesis; their results are unknown.

rationale_summary: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% with elevated inflation and a higher projected year-end path, lifting the dollar and pressuring long-duration, precious metals and high-beta cyclicals. Breadth is weak (14% of assets positive over 5 sessions) and dispersion is moderate at 2.37%. The sharp one-week hits to metals/mining, silver, copper, South Korea and South Africa came after solid prior-window relative trends, which fits a policy-shock overreaction more than fundamental deterioration; a partial mean-reversion into a data-light week is plausible but far from certain, so only a few candidates clear the bar.
portfolio_rationale: Post-hike shock hit high-beta EM and industrial-metals exposures that had positive prior relative trends; these are the cleanest overreaction candidates for a one-week bounce. South Korea combines the deepest active drawdown with a stabilizing local index; copper has a shallow 52-week-high gap and supportive volume; South Africa carries the strongest quality evidence. Metals/mining and silver were left just below the eligibility bar because the dollar and rate path remain live headwinds. Momentum-style continuation names (cybersecurity, oil) lack independent in-window support.
key_risks: A further hawkish repricing strengthens the dollar and extends the selloff in metals and EM equities; High-beta selections (EWY beta 3.24) magnify losses if US equities keep falling into the Sept 24 close; Sept 17 jobless claims, housing starts and Philly Fed, plus Sept 24 new-home sales, could shift rate expectations mid-window; Commodity weakness (Brent -2.7%) may reflect demand deterioration rather than temporary overreaction

rationale_summary: Hawkish surprise: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with 10y at 5.01% and dollar up 1.5% over five sessions; SPY down 2.4% over 21 sessions with only 14% of assets positive. Strong-dollar, higher-rate regime pressured metals, EM, and crypto in the latest window, but the Kospi rose 1.4% on Sep 16 and Europe/Asia rose broadly, suggesting some of the sharp EM/metals selloff is positioning rather than fundamental. Oil remains supported by prior trend but Brent fell 2.7%. Edge is modest; most candidates near coin-flip versus SPY.
portfolio_rationale: Ranked the sharp EM/industrial-metal pullbacks with intact prior relative trends (South Korea, copper, South Africa) as modest overreaction candidates, supported by Kospi and broad Asia gains on Sep 16 while US indexes fell. Edges are small and near the 55% threshold; hawkish Fed and strong dollar keep conviction low, so SPY is a reasonable default diagnostically.
key_risks: Continued dollar strength after the Fed hike extends EM and commodity underperformance; High-beta candidates (EWY beta 3.2, XME beta 1.6) amplify any further US equity drawdown; Jobless claims, housing, and industrial production releases could shift rate expectations mid-window; Copper and mining reversal fails if the prior window's selloff reflects genuine China-linked demand weakness
